subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Journalism: Who Wrote This Article?
description: A short lesson to help you apply AI Journalism: Who Wrote This Article?.

hook.text: Sports scores, earnings reports, weather summaries — millions of articles are already written by AI.

buildup.text: Automated journalism handles templated, data-driven stories that follow predictable patterns.

discovery.text: The Associated Press uses AI to generate thousands of earnings reports per quarter.

twist.text: Readers trust 'journalist' bylines. Some outlets use AI without disclosure.

climax.text: CNET published AI articles with errors that damaged its credibility when discovered.

punchline.text: AI writes fast. Trust erodes faster when the byline lies.

quiz.question: What risk does undisclosed AI journalism create?
options: Eroded trust when AI-written errors are discovered

details.summary: News organizations use AI to generate earnings reports, sports recaps, and breaking news alerts. Readers often cannot tell whether a human or machine wrote the article they are reading.
details.whyItMatters: AI journalism raises trust concerns. If readers cannot distinguish machine-written from human-written news, transparency about AI use becomes essential for maintaining credibility.
takeaways: AI writes news articles for major publications today
Readers often cannot distinguish AI text from human writing
Transparency policies are needed to maintain public trust

faq.question: Which news organizations use AI to write articles?
faq.answer: The Associated Press, Bloomberg, Reuters, and others use AI for formulaic content like earnings reports and sports recaps. AI handles data-heavy stories that follow predictable templates.

faq.question: Should AI-written articles be labeled as such?
faq.answer: Most journalism ethics experts say yes. Readers deserve to know how their news was produced, and transparency helps maintain the trust that journalism depends on.
